ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Focal respiratory findings with fever

A previously healthy 5-year-old has fever, cough and right-sided abdominal pain. Respiratory rate is 42/min. Examination shows reduced air entry and focal crackles at the right base, with no abdominal guarding. Which diagnosis best unifies the findings?

  1. Right lower-lobe pneumonia
  2. Acute appendicitis
  3. Viral gastroenteritis
  4. Acute cystitis
  5. Intussusception
Answer and explanation

Right lower-lobe pneumonia

Lower-lobe inflammation can cause referred abdominal pain; tachypnea and focal lung findings identify the likely source.

Option explanations

Right lower-lobe pneumonia: Lower-lobe inflammation can cause referred abdominal pain; tachypnea and focal lung findings identify the likely source.

Acute appendicitis: Appendicitis does not explain focal crackles and reduced basal air entry.

Viral gastroenteritis: There is no diarrhea or vomiting pattern, and focal respiratory findings require explanation.

Acute cystitis: Urinary infection would not explain the localized chest abnormalities.

Intussusception: Intussusception typically causes episodic abdominal symptoms rather than this febrile focal respiratory pattern.
